JUST IN: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., in a press briefing at the Palace on Monday (Aug. 11, 2025), unveils a website that will allow the public to access information on flood control projects, enabling citizens to identify and monitor projects in their area.

PBBM: We have put it into a form that is accessible to the public, and most importantly, it is in a form that the public can use so that they can first identify the… flood control projects that are within their area.

The President says the platform is intended to promote transparency and public participation by making project details easier to find and verify.

This follows the President’s directive during his fourth SONA to DPWH and other concerned agencies to submit a list of all flood control projects nationwide since the beginning of his term in mid-2022 as the gov’t mounts a sweeping audit.

Marcos says total cost of all of the projects since July 2022 is PHP545 billion.

Marcos flags "disturbing" information that 20 percent of the total PHP545 billion flood control projects budget was awarded to only 15 contractors. 

He encourages the public to visit the flood control website, adding that reports and complaints will go directly to him.

Marcos says he is not accusing any of the said contractors of wrongdoing, but noted that deeper probe is ongoing.

Marcos says businessman Ramon Ang's proposal to help solve flooding in Metro Manila is “certainly very welcome.” | Darryl John EsguerraJUST IN: President Ferdinand R.
